data.narrative:
Dronamics is a Series A-stage autonomous drone company founded by Svilen and Konstantin Rangelov. The valuation exercise draws from a sector comprising eight private peers—including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro—with no public comparables available. The fragmented stage and business model distribution within Drones & Autonomous limited the applicability of peer-median methods; a narrow same-stage peer set could not be constructed with sufficient density.

Stage-progression analysis proved the only methodologically sound triangulation approach. Using the $43.2M in total capital raised as a valuation proxy, a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage transitions yields an implied valuation of $86M. This method rests on the assumption that Dronamics' next funding event will command a doubling of effective enterprise value relative to cumulative invested capital—a conservative benchmark given the growth profile expected across this sector.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $73M to $99M, centered on $86M. Key uncertainties include the company's current traction metrics, path to revenue, and competitive positioning relative to the named peer set. The absence of a tight peer cohort at identical stage and scale means this range carries material estimation risk and should be weighted against operational milestones and market expansion data not captured in this quantitative frame.
